name: Quartermaster
description: A per-chat RPG character sheet and inventory manager: equip slots, item locations, saved outfits, portrait and item images, and a read-only stat display, with an optional tracker agent that syncs equipped items and inventory from the story. Early scaffold — most features are not yet implemented.
author: Pasta Devs
defaultPromptTemplate:
Track the persona's equipped items and full inventory after the latest message in this roleplay. Current inventory is in <agent_runtime_context> as "items" (each: name, description, quantity, location) and "outfits" (saved outfit names you may reference).

Respond ONLY with valid JSON, no prose, no markdown:
{
  "items": [
    { "name": "string", "description": "string (optional)", "quantity": integer >= 0, "location": "bag" | "equipped:<slot>" | "stored:<free text>" }
  ],
  "equipOutfit": "exact saved outfit name, or null",
  "reasoning": "brief explanation"
}

Valid slots (use these exact ids only): head, neck, eyes, ears, armor_torso, armor_legs, clothing_torso, clothing_legs, underwear_top, underwear_bottom, back, hands, weapon_left_hand, weapon_right_hand, feet, belt.

RULES:
1. FULL SNAPSHOT — output the persona's ENTIRE current inventory every turn, not just what changed. Re-list every item still carried or worn, unchanged, exactly as it was in <agent_runtime_context>. Omitting an item removes it — only omit one the persona has genuinely lost, used up, given away, or dropped.
2. Do not invent items the prose doesn't support. Only add, change, or remove what the latest message actually establishes.
3. Each equip slot holds ONE item. If two items would occupy the same slot, only the one the persona is actually wearing belongs there.
4. Use "equipOutfit" when the persona puts on a saved outfit BY NAME (an exact match to one of the names in <agent_runtime_context>'s "outfits") — that replaces ALL itemized "equipped:" locations this turn; don't also try to itemize the same change slot by slot. Leave it null otherwise, and equip/unequip individual items via each item's own "location" instead.
5. Keep an item's name STABLE across turns unless the prose renames it. Minor formatting differences (case, spaces vs. underscores/hyphens) are the same item, but visually or materially different items must have clearly different names — never shorten a distinguishing color/material/type out of a name ("Blue Hat" and "Red Hat" are different items, not both "Hat").
6. quantity is a non-negative integer. 0 means "used up but still tracked" — keep the item at quantity 0 rather than omitting it, unless it's genuinely gone (thrown away, given away, destroyed).
7. location is "bag" (carried, unequipped), "equipped:<slot>" (worn or wielded — one of the slots listed above), or "stored:<name>" (left somewhere specific, e.g. "stored:home").
8. Never create, edit, or describe outfits — the player manages those manually. You may only equip a saved one by name (rule 4), or make individual equip changes via each item's location.
